authority: a0/tasks/maxcut/INTERFACE.md §5 (cut_edges is the only authoritative value; cut_fraction is display only, read by no decision) read together with a0/contract/selection/simpleloop.selection.json (the frozen rule c*_t = argmax_{i<=t} E(c_i), exact comparison, lexicographic-id tie-break)
check_point: T1 A1: c*_t = argmax_{i<=t} cut_edges(Outcome supplied by the harness)

scalarization.nonfinite: cut_edges is an integer by construction (INTERFACE.md §5); a non-integer or a float that is not finite is rejected as an adapter-side error, never compared
scalarization.null_is_not_zero: a null scalar is never coerced to 0.0 or to -inf; an unscored candidate is recorded as unscored and excluded from the argmax. A non-ok Outcome carries no scalar at all (E* never writes 0 for a failure; c03 is the control: a legitimate 0 is a real 0).
scalarization.integer_authority: the returned scalar keeps the integer type of cut_edges, so the argmax is exact integer comparison rather than an IEEE-754 equality that merely happens to be exact at these magnitudes

selection.champion_update: running max over all candidates evaluated so far, so c*_t is monotone and never loses a previously best candidate
selection.epsilon_role: the frozen conformance epsilon is the A0.1 tolerance only; it is NOT applied in selection
selection.order_invariance: c*_t is a function of the set {(candidate_id, scalar)}; permuting the order in which candidates are proposed cannot change the champion
selection.rule: c*_t = argmax over { c_i : i <= t and scalar(c_i) is not null } of scalar(c_i)
selection.tie_break: smallest candidate_id by byte-wise comparison of the UTF-8 encoding of candidate_id
selection.when_nothing_scored: chosen_candidate_id is null; the run continues with parent = null and the iteration is recorded honestly
